title: How to Fix Squarespace Domain Forwarding Not Working 2026 Easily
description:
Here is How to Fix Squarespace Domain Forwarding Not Working 2026 Easily.

So, after setting up domain forwarding in Squarespace, you might expect it to start working right away — but sometimes, the redirect doesn’t kick in even after 15 or 30 minutes.

If that’s happening to you — here’s why, and what to do next.

First, don’t panic — this is completely normal.

Squarespace mentions that forwarding changes — especially with SSL enabled — may take up to 48 hours to fully propagate. But in most cases, it’s done within 1 to 2 hours.

So if it’s been just 30 minutes and you’re not seeing the redirect happen yet, give it a little more time.

Now, let’s do a few quick checks:

✅ Step 1 – Clear your browser cache.
Sometimes, your browser is still holding the old DNS or page data. Try opening your site in an incognito tab or clear your cache and reload.

✅ Step 2 – Try it on mobile or a different network.
If the redirect works elsewhere, it means your DNS is still updating locally.

✅ Step 3 – Check DNS records again.
Go to Settings - Domains - DNS Settings. Make sure there are no leftover A records or CNAMEs for the same subdomain you’re forwarding, like www. Even one leftover record can block forwarding from working.

✅ Step 4 – Confirm your rule was saved properly.
Go back to the Website - Forwarding section and double-check that your rule is listed, the correct URL is entered, and SSL is enabled if needed.

Still not working after an hour or two?

Try removing the forwarding rule, saving it, and then re-adding it from scratch. This can sometimes reset the redirect configuration.

And lastly — wait it out. Full DNS propagation with SSL can genuinely take a few hours depending on your ISP and location.

Conclusion:
Domain forwarding on Squarespace is easy — but it’s not instant. Give it some time, check for conflicts, and always verify your DNS and redirect rules.

Hope this helps! If your issue still isn’t resolved after a few hours, let me know in the comments, and I’ll help you dig deeper.

Thanks for watching.

title: How to Transfer Domain From Squarespace to Cloudflare Easily 2026
description:
Here is How to Transfer Domain From Squarespace to Cloudflare Easily 2026.

Welcome back to our guide! In today's video, we're going to walk you through how to transfer a domain from Squarespace to Cloudflare. Let's get started.
 

 First, log in to your Cloudflare account using your credentials. If you're new to Cloudflare, click on the sign-up option and follow the on-screen instructions to create an account.
 

 Transferring your domain from Squarespace to Cloudflare can be a strategic decision for several reasons. Cloudflare often offers competitive domain registration pricing, which can be more cost-effective than Squarespace. If you're looking to reduce costs, transferring to Cloudflare is a practical move. Additionally, if you're using Cloudflare for services like CDN (Content Delivery Network) or DNS management, consolidating your domain registration can simplify management by having everything in one place.
 

 Once you're in your Cloudflare dashboard, ensure your Squarespace domain is eligible for transfer. Typically, domains must be at least 60 days old and not recently transferred or renewed. Domain privacy protection services should be disabled for the transfer process. On the left side of your Cloudflare dashboard, hover over ""Domain Registration"" and click on ""Manage Domains."" Here, you'll see the option to transfer your domain. If the option isn't visible, you might need to verify your email to proceed with domain registration and transfers.
 

 Transferring a domain from Squarespace to Cloudflare is straightforward. You don't need to be tech-savvy, as the platform handles most technical aspects for you. Once your email is verified, follow the on-screen instructions to complete the transfer from Squarespace to Cloudflare.
 

 Alternatively, you can access your Squarespace website, navigate to the bottom left corner, click on ""Settings,"" and then ""Domains and Email."" Here, manage your domains from Squarespace or other sellers. If you don't have a domain yet, you can register one through Squarespace, but keep in mind the costs, which can start from $14 per year.
 

 Once you have your domain, you can initiate the transfer to Cloudflare. And that's it for today's video on how to transfer your domain from Squarespace to Cloudflare. Thank you for watching, and we'll see you again in the next one!
